finding: WHAT THIS PASS ADDS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT
detail: THE ARCHIVE ALREADY READ THE FIFTY. gedenkbuch-fifty.tsv, 20 September 2026, took names, dates and birthplaces off the five result pages and drew the finding that matters most — three of fifty born at Schubin, the rest clustered in Kreis Schlochau and Kreis Stolp, and Sally Leibholz born at Hammerstein in 1847 closing the loop. NONE OF THAT IS NEW HERE AND IT IS NOT RESTATED AS IF IT WERE. That file names its own gap in so many words: "what is NOT in this file — the deportation and death details of the forty-six". THIS PASS FILLS EXACTLY THAT GAP, and adds two people the surname search had never reached.

finding: HOW THE DETAIL WAS GOT, WITHOUT OPENING FIFTY PAGES
detail: The search form has an EXPORT AS CSV control. The file was not downloaded; the same request was made in the page and the response decoded in memory — it is windows-1252, not UTF-8, and reading it as UTF-8 mangles every umlaut. It returns EIGHTEEN COLUMNS per person: birth name, Geburtskreis, Geburtsland, borough of residence, Abschiebung nach Polen, Inhaftierung, Emigration, the town deported from, both deportation legs with dates, Schicksal, place of death and date of death. All fifty are now in leibholz-gedenkbuch.tsv, which held four.

finding: THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS HALF RIGHT, AND THE WRONG HALF IS THE USEFUL PART
detail: Worklist row 246 expected "forty-six people with Berlin addresses, and a Berlin address can be laid against the directory the way the Weinstraße household already was". FORTY-FOUR OF THE FIFTY DO LIVE IN BERLIN — Schöneberg 6, Wilmersdorf 6, Charlottenburg 5, Friedrichshain 5, Tiergarten 4, Neukölln 4, Mitte 4, Prenzlauer Berg 3, Kreuzberg 1, three plain "Berlin", two with two boroughs — BUT THE GEDENKBUCH RECORDS THE BOROUGH AND NOT THE STREET. A borough will not find a household in the Adressbuch; it will only say which pages are worth reading. The directory work row 246 imagined is still to be done and is larger than the row supposed.

finding: FOURTEEN OF THE FIFTY ARE MARRIED WOMEN INDEXED UNDER THE BIRTH NAME
detail: Bernstein, Bodin, Czarlinski, Dukelsky, Feldtmann, Heinrich, Kamnitzer, Meyer, Nehemias, Oliven, Simon, Stahl, Struzik and Weile are in the fifty because Leibholz is their GEBURTSNAME. This is a property of the instrument, not of the family: a surname search of the Gedenkbuch reaches women who never bore the name in life, and it would equally miss a Leibholz woman whose birth name was not recorded. IT APPLIES TO EVERY OTHER SURNAME THIS ARCHIVE HAS PUT TO THAT BOX.

finding: TWO DEATHS ARE RECORDED AS FREITOD
detail: Betty Leibholz née Pollack, born 5 August 1902, of Charlottenburg, died at Berlin on 23 DECEMBER 1935 — the earliest death in the fifty, and before the deportations began. And Gertrud Leibholz née Leibke, born 13 July 1894, of Wilmersdorf, died at Berlin on 27 FEBRUARY 1943, THE DAY AFTER JACOB LEIBHOLZ WAS DEPORTED TO AUSCHWITZ ON 26 FEBRUARY 1943. THE ARCHIVE DOES NOT CLAIM THE TWO ARE CONNECTED and holds no document joining Gertrud to Jacob. The date is recorded because the Fabrikaktion began on 27 February 1943, which is the ordinary explanation and the one to test before any other.

Chanah Chana Leibholz, born in BERLIN on 3 November 1937, of Friedrichshain, deported to Auschwitz on 3 MARCH 1943, aged five years and four months. Her parents are not named in the entry. She is the youngest of the fifty-two.

finding: SIX OF THE FIFTY ARE NOT BERLIN AT ALL
detail: Arthur (b. 27.06.1881 at Karwen) and Charlotte née Tworoger at HAMBURG, both to Minsk on 8 November 1941. Leo and Ida née Neuwahl at FRANKFURT AM MAIN, who EMIGRATED TO THE NETHERLANDS ON 13 FEBRUARY 1937 and were taken from Westerbork to Sobibor on 23 March 1943 — the only emigration in the fifty, and it did not save them. Else Oliven née Leibholz at Dortmund and Düsseldorf. And Heinz Paul Hugo, born in Berlin in 1922, whose residence is given as the UMSCHULUNGSLAGER GRÜNER WEG AT PADERBORN before Neukölln — a forced-labour retraining camp, a residence only in the sense the Gedenkbuch means it.

finding: FOUR RECORDS THAT LOOK LIKE DUPLICATES ARE NOT
detail: Two men named ARTHUR LEIBHOLZ (born 2 January 1878 at Hammerstein, of Schöneberg; born 27 June 1881 at Karwen, of Hamburg) and two named WILHELM LEIBHOLZ (born 28 December 1890 at Glowitz, of Neukölln; born 15 December 1904 at Tempelburg, of Friedrichshain). The evidence builder keys a person on the name, so each pair shares one heading while keeping both records. The status column on all four says outright that they are namesakes and not duplicates, because a memorial is the last place to let two people collapse into one.

finding: *** TWO MORE VICTIMS, UNDER A SPELLING NOBODY HAD TRIED ***
detail: LAIBHOLZ returns TWO, and neither is any of the fifty. GEORG LAIBHOLZ, born 1 January 1883, of Berlin, died at Auschwitz — NOT Georg Leibholz born 7 June 1884 at Hammerstein, who went to Litzmannstadt and Kulmhof. LIDIA LAIBHOLZ, born 1884 with no day or month, of Berlin, died at Auschwitz — NOT Lydia Leibholz née Perl born 16 January 1885 at Bischofstein, who also went to Litzmannstadt and Kulmhof. Both Laibholz entries are thin: no birthplace, no borough, no date of death, which is what a record reconstructed from a transport list looks like rather than from a residence card. WHETHER LAIBHOLZ IS A CLERK'S SPELLING OF LEIBHOLZ OR A SEPARATE NAME IS NOT SETTLED BY THIS and no relationship is claimed. They are in the file because two murdered people with almost our surname were sitting one vowel away from every search this archive had run.

Ten put to the box on 22 September 2026. LEIBHOLZ 50 · LAIBHOLZ 2 · LEIBHOLD 1, which is a FALSE POSITIVE — the entry is "Passau, Leibhold", where Leibhold is the man's FORENAME and Passau the surname · LEIBHOLTZ, LEIPHOLZ, LEIBOLZ, LEBHOLZ, LEIHOLZ, LEIBHOLCZ and LELBHOLZ all NOTHING. The Leipholz zero confirms at a second sitting what gedenkbuch-fifty.tsv found on 20 September.

finding: *** THE INSTRUMENT FAULT, WHICH NEARLY PUBLISHED FIVE FABRICATED NEGATIVES ***
detail: PRESSING RETURN IN THAT SEARCH BOX DOES NOT SUBMIT THE FORM. Five terms were typed and entered in succession and all five read back as "50 Results" — every one of them the previous page, unchanged, because nothing had been sent. Had the terms been rarer the readings would have looked like five ordinary negatives and gone into this archive as five facts that were never tested. IT WAS CAUGHT ONLY BECAUSE "50" IS NOT A BELIEVABLE ANSWER FOR FIVE DIFFERENT MISSPELLINGS. Re-run with a click on the Start search button, the same five gave 0, 50, 0, 1 and 0. THE RULE: on this form click the button, and interleave the control term so that every reading is a CHANGE of state and never a state.
